observation.visible_scene: A low-angle close-up of an illuminated ceiling lamp against a featureless black background. The lamp consists of a white, glossy dome shade seen as an oval, a dark circular socket ring at its center, and a glowing warm-white bulb hanging just below the socket. A faint diagonal shadow streak and a small bright reflection near the top edge of the shade are visible throughout.
visible_changes: The white shade drifts in position within the frame over time: it sits roughly centered-left in the early frames, shifts leftward during the middle section, and ends up right-of-center and higher in the later frames.

Motion blur appears intermittently, strongest in the middle frames (roughly the 12th–19th and 25th–30th samples), while the shade is comparatively sharp at the start and end of the excerpt, indicating periods of faster relative movement.
The apparent tilt and elongation of the oval shade change from frame to frame, consistent with a changing viewing angle rather than the shade itself deforming.

The bulb remains lit and attached to the central socket the whole time; its offset from the socket ring varies (sometimes hanging clearly below it, sometimes overlapping it), tracking the changing angle.
The background stays uniformly black with no other objects, so the shade and bulb are the only moving/visible entities.
The relative layout of shade, socket ring, and bulb is preserved as a single unit; no part separates or disappears.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiates or stops the motion (the excerpt begins and ends mid-motion).
Whether the apparent motion comes from a handheld camera panning/tilting or from the fixture itself swinging.
The lamp's true mounting and surroundings, which are out of frame.
uncertain_details: Because the background is pure black with no reference points, it cannot be determined whether the position drift and blur are camera movement or object movement.
The exact oscillation pattern or period of the apparent sway is not reliably measurable from these samples.
Minor changes in bulb position relative to the socket may be projection/angle effects rather than physical movement of the bulb.
